Neither set states a blade length in the text layer; the 135 m value is not supported anywhere on the page (the Z-coordinate axis runs to about 130 m), and the 130 m claim is an inference from the plot axis rather than a stated dimension. Both sets also repeat the spar cap and trailing edge reinforcement material facts three times each and treat figure shading ('green/blue shading') as a physical thickness value, which is a visualization convention, not a thickness. Important facts both sets miss: the main and aft shear webs are shown in red in Figure 14, and the modal frequencies in Table 6 (standstill, HAWCStab2) are referenced but not extracted.

variant-first.note: Set A and Set B contain the same 17 claims with identical values, conditions and quotes; only the ordering of two trailing-edge claims differs. Both correctly capture the spar cap (pultruded carbon unidirectional), outer skin (triaxial), trailing edge reinforcement (unidirectional glass), shear web sandwich construction, the ~50% span aft shear web and the edgewise uniaxial glass. Both also share the same defects: three 'thickness = shading colour' claims that turn a figure legend into a value, and two blade-length claims (135 m and 130 m) whose quotes are only axis labels/tick marks and do not support the values.
variant-first.remarks: The two sets are content-identical, so the comparison is a tie. Shared issues: 'thickness | green/blue shading' claims misbind a legend colour to a thickness value (3 per set); 'blade length 135 m' is supported only by the axis label 'Z-coordinate [m]' and 'length 130 m' reads an axis tick (130) as a length — the two length claims also contradict each other. Material facts are duplicated three times for spar caps and twice for trailing edge reinforcement under slightly different entity names. Both sets omit the modal-frequency fact (Table 6, first 10 frequencies at standstill) and the BECAS/HAWCStab2/BeamDyn modelling facts, though those may belong to other claim categories.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are nearly identical in content and quality, sharing the same claims about the VVC, the polarizers in the beam train, the telescope architecture, and the schematic layouts. Set B additionally includes the supported claim that higher topological charge yields a larger IWA, which Set A omits despite it being a key trade-off stated on the page. Both sets contain a duplicated VVC 'type' claim (phase-based coronagraph / phase-based) and a duplicated polarizer-in-beam-train claim, and both include label-only claims from the figures with trivial quotes. No claim in either set is misread or invented relative to the page text and figures.
baseline-first.remarks: The only differentiator is B's IWA-vs-topological-charge claim ('the higher the charge... the larger the IWA'), which is directly supported by the text and is an important design trade-off; A's omission of it counts against A. Both sets repeat the VVC type claim and the polarizer inclusion claim under two names. The 'Dichroic -> DM2 -> Polarizers -> Polarizers -> IFS' sequence in both sets compresses the schematic and skips the mask/stops/filter wheel/camera selector, so it reads as a loose ordering rather than a faithful path; it is shared, so it does not affect the comparison. Figure 5.5-15 label claims (CCD, DM1, DM2, IFS, OAP 5 in the blue channel) are supported by the image but stated with bare-label quotes.

variant-first.note: Set A and Set B share 18 essentially identical claims, but A adds one further correct and important claim: higher topological charge gives a larger IWA, with a supporting quote from the text. Both sets capture the VVC type/aperture/charge trade-offs, the off-axis monolith telescope, the polarizer purpose, and the Figure 5.5-14b/5.5-15 layout items. Both repeat the VVC 'phase-based' fact under two attribute names and both assert a 'Camera Selector to LOWFS' connection that the schematic does not show (LOWFS taps off near the coronagraph mask, well upstream of the camera selector). Because A includes the IWA trade-off that B omits, A is slightly better.
variant-first.remarks: The 'Camera Selector -> LOWFS' connection appears in both sets but Figure 5.5-14b places LOWFS under the beam between the polarizers and the coronagraph mask, with only Camera Selector -> Camera and Camera Selector -> IFS shown at the right end; arrow routing in the small schematic is somewhat hard to resolve, hence medium confidence. Both sets also miss the definition of topological charge (number of full 2π radian cycles of the vortex phase ramp) and the statement that the VVC family gave the most favorable IWA/low-order-aberration trade-off among the four families considered. Several figure-label claims (CCD, DM1, DM2, IFS, OAP 5) are supported by Figure 5.5-15 but carry only the bare label as quote, and the two 'component sequence' claims are partial subsequences of the schematic rather than complete paths.

variant-first.remarks: Both sets repeat the finish-floor and int.-step facts under two attribute names (elevation vs height), so each has 2 redundant claims out of 17. baseline-first.note: Both sets contain the same seven claims with the same values, bindings and supporting quotes: FFA-W3 airfoil family, Re = 8E+6 to 18E+6, the 30%/70% turbulent/transition polar mix, the 48% interpolation threshold, and the blade root cylinder's Cl = 0.0 and Cd = 0.35. The only difference is that Set B adds 'Section 6' as a condition on the two polar-mix ratio claims, which is merely a cross-reference to where the polars are presented rather than an engineering condition; Set A omits it. Neither set misreads or invents anything, and both omit the same facts (e.g. the Snel/Du-Selig 3D corrections), so the sets are effectively equivalent.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets miss the page's statements that the WindIO/report airfoil data exclude an engineering 3D flow correction, that HAWC2 applies the Snel correction by default, and that OpenFAST input files use the Du-Selig correction; these are arguably important engineering facts. Set B's 'conditions: Section 6' is a bibliographic cross-reference, not a real condition, and is best treated as noise rather than an error.

variant-first.note: Both sets contain the same seven claims with the same values, bindings and supporting quotes, and all are faithful to the page. Both sets also omit several notable facts on the page (360-degree polars extrapolated with AirfoilPreppy, the Snel and Du-Selig 3D corrections, the EllipSys2D CFD basis), so the omission is shared and does not separate them.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts (FFA-W3 family, EllipSys2D, cylinder Cl/Cd, linear interpolation above 48% thickness, Snel in HAWC2, Du-Selig in OpenFAST, no 3D correction in the data). On balance B is better: it adds two correct, engineering-relevant facts at the cost of one wrong duplicate, while A leaves the mixing ratio out.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets repeat the 'aeroelastic simulations | airfoil data source' fact twice (once with and once without the EllipSys2D detail). variant-first.note: Both sets share the same 10 core claims (airfoil family, EllipSys2D, cylinder Cl/Cd, interpolation above 48% thickness, 3D correction models, no 3D correction in WindIO/report), and both repeat the airfoil-data-source fact twice. variant-first.note: Both sets share the same core claims and both misbind the HLC's TRL 5 and WFIRST CGI traceability to the VVC, so each has two wrong claims. Set B adds four correct claims (focal plane mask and mask wheel at the focal point, the parabolic mirror's beam-convergence function, and the M3 collimated input light), while Set A's only unique claim is the optical-train sequence, which is correct but partially duplicated by B's component claims. Set B therefore captures more of the page's engineering content without adding errors, though its mask-location claims are of marginal value. Both sets omit the charge-6 immunity-to-low-order-aberrations trade-off and the Table 5.5-6 aberration-sensitivity data.
variant-first.remarks: The TRL 5 and WFIRST CGI traceability statements in the source clearly attach to the HLC ('the HLC is also considered as a backup due to its high technology readiness (TRL 5) and traceability to the WFIRST CGI'), yet both extractions bind them to the VVC — a shared systematic error worth flagging. Both sets also miss the stated charge-6 trade-off partner (immunity to low-order aberrations: tip-tilt, defocus, astigmatism, coma, spherical) and the Table 5.5-6 caption content (aberration sensitivity, charge 4 to 10, 2e-11 raw starlight suppression at 2.5-3.5 lambda/D). Claims like 'VVC IWA = small' and 'layout simplicity = high' are qualitative and of limited engineering use; the source lists 'layout simplicity' without the qualifier 'high'.

baseline-first.note: Both sets share the same core claims and the same misbinding: TRL 5 and traceability to WFIRST CGI are attributed to the VVC, but the text assigns both to the HLC ("the HLC is also considered as a backup due to its high technology readiness (TRL 5) and traceability to the WFIRST CGI"). Set A adds four further supported claims (focal plane masks at the focal point, mask wheel at the focal point, parabolic mirror converging the beam, collimated light from M3 as input), while Set B replaces them with one compound optical-train sequence claim whose quote is stitched with ellipses. Minor: 'layout simplicity | high' adds a qualifier ('high') not present in the text ('layout simplicity'); treated as acceptable paraphrase rather than an error. Both sets omit the charge-6 immunity to low-order aberrations (tip-tilt, defocus, astigmatism, coma, spherical) and the Table 5.5-6 aberration-sensitivity data. The table caption in the text layer is garbled ("2e 11" = 2×10⁻¹¹, "2 5 3 5 λ/D" = 2.5–3.5 λ/D), and the last sentence is cut off at "a second parabolic".

variant-first.note: Both sets extract the same core facts correctly — the reference keynote codes (BOOSTER PUMP 22 11 23, DOMESTIC WATER PIPING 22 11 16, HTP SUPERSTOR SOLAR WATER TANK 22 33 00, SOLAR PUMP STATION 23 56 01, DISHWASHER 11 31 13.A7), the C1 drawing scale 1/2"=1'-0", and the ground-plane elevations — and both share the same defects: four invented 'location' claims (lower right / upper vertical / central / lower left assembly) that the page never states, several vague 'system'/'plumbing system' component-identifier claims, and repeated facts (CEILING FINISH elevation stated twice, keynote codes stated again under generic names). variant-first.remarks: The four 'location' claims (e.g. 'component 22 33 00 | location | lower right assembly') have no textual support anywhere on the page and use an undefined 'assembly' vocabulary; they should be dropped or replaced by verifiable section/detail references. The generic entities ('system', 'plumbing system', 'Water Supply System') are misbound or vague: 22 11 23.A2 is SUMP PUMP and 22 41 23.B3 is PRE-FABRICATED SHOWER STALL per the Reference Keynotes, so binding them to 'Water Supply System'/'plumbing system' is wrong. Elevation values are given as feet-inches (e.g. 2'-0 3/8") but tagged with unit 'ft', which double-states the unit. Both sets miss the three General Sheet Notes and the named keynotes CLOTHES WASHER, SUMP PUMP, PRE-FABRICATED SHOWER STALL, FACILITY SANITARY SEWERAGE and the A1 (WASTE WATER LONGITUDINAL SECTION) scale.
